andhraPradesh.headline: Mee Bhoomi–Mee Hakku: AP reports 16 lakh acres removed from Section 22-A prohibited list
facts: At a Gram Sabha in Panduvaripeta, P. Gannavaram constituency, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district, the Chief Minister participated in the state’s Mee Bhoomi–Mee Hakku programme.
The Chief Minister said 16 lakh acres had been removed from the Section 22-A prohibited properties list after corrections to land records; this is an official claim reported from the event.
The government said resurveys were completed in 8,234 villages and over 36 lakh pattadar passbooks had been distributed.
The stated target is to complete surveys in 8,582 villages and distribute 56 lakh passbooks by March 2027.
The programme addresses land-record accuracy, property rights and access to land transactions.
andhraPradesh.summary: At the September 9 Gram Sabha in Konaseema, the government presented progress on land-record correction and pattadar-passbook distribution under Mee Bhoomi–Mee Hakku. The reported figures and March 2027 target are government statements; the source does not establish that the remaining survey or passbook work is complete. ([newkerala.com](https://www.newkerala.com/news/a/people-friendly-coalition-govt-committed-welfare-development-good-governance-489.htm?utm_source=openai))
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Land records, property rights, registration restrictions and digital governance.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Section 22-A of the Registration Act concerns properties prohibited from registration; distinguish reported removal of land from the prohibited list from a general land-title guarantee.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how accurate land records, accessible grievance redress and transparent re-surveys can strengthen tenure security while reducing disputes and transaction barriers.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct state and district connection: the event took place in Panduvaripeta, Konaseema district, under an Andhra Pradesh land-record programme.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh rainfall deficit reaches 54.7% through September 8
facts: The Times of India reported cumulative rainfall of 209.4 mm in Andhra Pradesh from June 1 to September 8, against a normal 462.7 mm: a 54.7% deficit.
The report identified the largest district deficits as Annamayya (78.3%), Prakasam (67.1%), Chittoor (65%), Sri Sathya Sai (61.8%) and Visakhapatnam (60.8%).
As of September 2, 52.84 lakh acres had been sown, reported as 69% of the normal cropped area.
Previous: reporting based on data through September 5 put the rainfall deficit at 46%. Today: the September 9 report, using data through September 8, put it at 54.7%.
The figures indicate continuing risks to kharif cultivation and water availability; the rainfall report does not itself establish crop-loss totals.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: the earlier report cited a 46% deficit through September 5. Today: the September 9 update reported a 54.7% deficit through September 8, with substantial shortfalls in several districts. The sowing figure is separately dated September 2 and should not be treated as a September 9 acreage count. ([newindianexpress.com](https://www.newindianexpress.com/amp/story/states/andhra-pradesh/2026/Sep/08/el-ni%C3%B1o-reshapes-andhra-pradeshs-weather-disrupts-sw-monsoon?utm_source=openai))
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Southwest monsoon, rainfall departures, drought vulnerability and rain-fed agriculture.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Rainfall departure is measured against the normal for the same period; compare figures only when their reporting periods and normal baselines are stated.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how rainfall deficits affect crop choice, irrigation demand and rural livelihoods, and evaluate district-level contingency planning and water conservation.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP-specific link: the update reports state and district rainfall deficits and kharif sowing in Andhra Pradesh.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh outlines power-supply roadmap with thermal procurement and storage
facts: At an AP Power Co-ordination Committee meeting in Vijayawada on September 8, the Energy Department outlined a roadmap for reliable round-the-clock power supply.
The proposal includes procuring 1,600 MW of thermal baseload power through tariff-based competitive bidding on a DBFOO framework, with proposed contract terms of 12–25 years.
The report also described deployment of 1,500 MW/6,000 MWh of battery energy storage and plans for more than 2,000 MW of battery and pumped-hydro storage projects.
DISCOMs were directed to prepare a 12-month advance power-supply plan.
The reported procurement and storage plans are proposals/planning measures, not evidence that the capacity is already operational.
andhraPradesh.summary: The state outlined a generation-and-storage planning response to rising demand and peak-period supply needs. The reported thermal procurement and storage capacities remain planned measures; the source does not report completed procurement or operational commissioning. ([newindianexpress.com](https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/vijayawada/2026/Sep/09/andhra-government-draws-247-power-plan-amid-el-ni%C3%B1o-demand?utm_source=openai))
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Electricity-sector planning, competitive bidding, energy storage and grid balancing.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: DBFOO means Design, Build, Finance, Own and Operate; battery storage can shift surplus daytime solar power toward evening demand.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Evaluate the trade-offs between thermal baseload procurement and storage-led flexibility, including cost, reliability, emissions and procurement risks.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP-specific link: the roadmap was presented at the state Power Co-ordination Committee meeting in Vijayawada and concerns AP’s power system.

andhraPradesh.headline: NTR district’s RISE initiative featured in national livelihoods-and-skilling webinar
facts: The Rural Incubation, Skilling and Entrepreneurship (RISE) initiative in NTR district was featured in the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship’s Skill Manthan webinar on September 9.

The district report describes the RISE centre at Guntupalli as supporting rural women’s skills and entrepreneurship under a “One Family-One Entrepreneur” vision.
The initiative was reported as being implemented with support from NITI Aayog, SERP and other partners.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh urban-governance experience slated for presentation at IFAT India 2026
facts: A September 9 report said Andhra Pradesh’s Municipal Administration and Urban Development Principal Secretary was scheduled to participate in IFAT India 2026 in Mumbai.
The conference was scheduled for September 9–11 at the Bombay Exhibition Centre.
The planned session concerned municipal service delivery for sustainable sanitation and was part of a wider discussion on urban sanitation priorities.

The report said AP would present experience in civic reforms, solid-waste management and sustainable urban services, including initiatives associated with Swachh Bharat Mission 2.0 and Swarna Andhra–Swachha Andhra.

national.headline: Cabinet approves eight railway multitracking projects across nine states
facts: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved five projects costing about ₹10,021 crore across Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Telangana.
The five projects add about 540 km of track; the Arakkonam–Renigunta third and fourth lines account for 77 km.
The southern package is planned for completion by 2029–30 and is expected to connect about 2,121 villages with a population of roughly 52 lakh.
A separate three-project package costing ₹10,783 crore adds about 656 km across West Bengal, Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
The projects are planned under PM Gati Shakti; the eastern package is expected to serve about 4,790 villages and add 27 million tonnes per year of freight capacity.
national.summary: On 9 September, the Cabinet approved two railway multitracking packages covering eight projects. The southern package includes the Arakkonam–Renigunta line, giving the decision a direct Andhra Pradesh connectivity link; the projects remain approved works, not completed infrastructure.
national.staticLink: Railway infrastructure, multimodal connectivity and logistics; PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish the two approvals: five projects/about 540 km in the south and three/about 656 km in eastern and central India; both target completion by 2029–30.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how capacity expansion on congested rail routes can improve freight efficiency, regional connectivity and lower-emission transport, while considering implementation and land-acquisition challenges.
national.apLink: The Arakkonam–Renigunta third and fourth line is a 77-km project connecting with Renigunta in Andhra Pradesh.

national.headline: India and ASEAN set cooperation priorities at ninth agriculture and forestry ministerial meeting
facts: The ninth ASEAN–India Ministerial Meeting on Agriculture and Forestry was held in New Delhi on 9 September 2026.
It was co-chaired by India’s Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and the Philippines’ Agriculture Secretary Francisco P. Tiu Laurel.
The meeting identified climate-resilient agriculture, low-emission rice, water productivity, digital agriculture, soil health, food safety and resilient value chains as cooperation priorities.
Ministers welcomed the ASEAN Food, Agriculture and Forestry Sectoral Plan 2026–2030 and looked forward to implementing an ASEAN–India medium-term action plan for 2026–2030.
The tenth ministerial meeting is to be convened in 2028.
national.summary: The ministerial meeting reinforced ASEAN–India cooperation on food security, sustainable agriculture and forestry. Its agenda links agricultural technology and research cooperation with climate resilience, water management and stronger regional value chains.
national.staticLink: ASEAN–India relations; regional cooperation in agriculture, food security and sustainable development.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The meeting was the ninth ASEAN–India Agriculture and Forestry ministerial; the next is planned for 2028, with cooperation priorities including low-emission rice and digital agriculture.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how regional agricultural cooperation can strengthen food-system resilience and climate adaptation, while addressing the need for equitable technology and knowledge sharing.

national.headline: India and Sri Lanka sign defence cooperation MoUs during Raksha Mantri’s Colombo visit
facts: India and Sri Lanka exchanged MoUs during Defence Minister Rajnath Singh’s visit to Colombo on 9 September 2026.
One MoU covers the upgrade of six L70 guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force under a Government of India grant.
The two sides also signed MoUs for cooperation between their National Cadet Corps and National Defence Colleges.
Three Bailey bridges constructed by Indian Defence Forces were virtually inaugurated during the visit.
The L70 upgrade is intended to strengthen Sri Lanka’s air-defence architecture; the MoU does not mean the upgrades are already complete.
national.summary: The visit produced defence and institutional cooperation agreements, including a grant-backed MoU to upgrade six L70 guns previously supplied to Sri Lanka. The two countries also advanced NCC youth exchanges and defence-college knowledge sharing.
national.staticLink: India’s neighbourhood policy, maritime security and bilateral defence cooperation.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The L70 agreement concerns six Sri Lankan Air Force guns and is supported by an Indian government grant; NCC and National Defence College cooperation were also covered.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how defence assistance, institutional exchanges and infrastructure support contribute to India’s security partnerships in the Indian Ocean neighbourhood.

national.headline: Centre announces farmer consultation before finalising proposed stricter Seed Act
facts: On 9 September, the Union Agriculture Ministry said it was preparing a new Seed Act to address fake and substandard seeds.
A consultation with farmer organisations was scheduled for 10 September 2026 at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi, before the draft is finalised.
The proposed law is expected to provide stronger penalties, potentially including imprisonment, for sale of fake, adulterated or substandard seeds.
The government said the draft would consider end-to-end traceability and protection of farmers’ rights over traditional seeds.
As of the announcement, the proposal was not an enacted Act or a Bill passed by Parliament.
national.summary: The Centre announced a consultation as part of preparing a proposed stricter seed law. The stated aims include improving seed quality and traceability while safeguarding traditional seeds; the legislative proposal had not yet become law.
national.staticLink: Seed regulation, agricultural inputs, farmer rights and legislative process.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Classify the proposed Seed Act as a pre-legislative proposal announced for consultation—not an enacted law or passed Bill.
national.mainsAngle: Evaluate how seed-quality regulation can protect farmers and food security, while balancing enforcement, due process, market access and farmers’ rights over traditional seeds.

national.headline: ICMR researchers report India’s first genome-wide association study on endometriosis
facts: ICMR–National Institute for Research on Women’s Health researchers reported India’s first genome-wide association study (GWAS) on genetic susceptibility to endometriosis among Indian women.
The multicentre study involved 18 centres and was conducted under the Endometriosis Clinical and Genetic Research in India initiative.

The study was published in Scientific Reports under the title “Genome-wide association analysis of endometriosis in Indian women supports shared genetic susceptibility and suggestive population-specific signals.”
AIIMS Raipur enrolled 400 participants over four years: 200 endometriosis patients and 200 controls.
Researchers said the findings provide baseline data for further work on disease risk, diagnosis and treatment; they do not establish a standalone diagnostic test.
national.summary: The ICMR-led study addresses a gap in genetic research on endometriosis among Indian women and drew participants from diverse regional and socioeconomic backgrounds. Its findings may support future research into risk identification and care, including for populations often underrepresented in research.
national.staticLink: Women’s health, genomics, non-communicable conditions and health-research equity.
national.prelimsTakeaway: GWAS means genome-wide association study; the reported Indian study was conducted by ICMR–NIRWoH through an 18-centre collaboration.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss the role of representative health research in improving women’s health policy, while addressing research inclusion, privacy and translation of genomic evidence into accessible care.

national.headline: Ninth Rashtriya Poshan Maah launched for nationwide nutrition activities
facts: The Ministry of Women and Child Development launched the ninth Rashtriya Poshan Maah on 9 September 2026 in Varanasi.
The month-long campaign runs from 9 September to 8 October 2026 under the theme “Hamari Anganwadi, Hamari Jimmedari”.
Focus areas include dietary diversity, adequate protein, fresh hot-cooked meals at Anganwadi centres, community ownership and early-childhood nutrition and stimulation.
The launch also highlighted 10 years of the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana.
The ministry reported that more than 14 lakh Anganwadi centres serve over 7.5 crore children and 1.10 crore pregnant and lactating women.

national.headline: First INNOPROM India opens as India and Russia pursue industrial cooperation
facts: The first INNOPROM India was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from 9 to 11 September 2026.
The event brought together government, manufacturing, technology, investor and industry representatives from India and Russia.
The stated focus areas included manufacturing, industrial technology, localisation, investment and business partnerships.
India and Russia set a bilateral trade target of ₹9.45 lakh crore (US$100 billion) by 2030.
NICDC highlighted 20 industrial smart cities across 13 states with stated investment potential of ₹5.35 lakh crore; this is potential, not realised investment.
national.summary: The inaugural INNOPROM India provided a platform for India–Russia industrial and technology engagement. The announced 2030 bilateral trade target and industrial-corridor investment potential are goals and opportunities, not completed trade or investments.
national.staticLink: India–Russia strategic partnership, industrial corridors, manufacturing and foreign trade.
national.prelimsTakeaway: INNOPROM India 2026 was the inaugural India edition, scheduled for 9–11 September in New Delhi; distinguish targets and potential from realised outcomes.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how industrial exhibitions and corridor infrastructure can support technology partnerships and manufacturing, while evaluating the gap between investment potential and actual project delivery.

national.headline: Centre announces launch of DILRMP 3.0 guidelines and a ₹565.50-crore land-records programme
facts: On 9 September, the Department of Land Resources announced that operational guidelines for DILRMP 3.0 (2026–2031) would be launched on 10 September.
The programme was described as a five-year Central Sector Scheme with an anticipated outlay of ₹565.50 crore.
The announced direction shifts from digitising records alone towards a GIS-enabled “Land Stack”.
The Department of Land Resources is to implement the programme across States and Union Territories.
On 9 September, the guidelines had been announced for the following day; the programme’s launch had not yet occurred.
national.summary: The Department of Land Resources announced a next-day launch of DILRMP 3.0 operational guidelines and outlined a five-year, GIS-oriented land-record modernisation programme. The 9 September development was an announcement, not the launch itself.
national.staticLink: Land governance, digital public infrastructure, land-record modernisation and Centre–State administration.
national.prelimsTakeaway: DILRMP stands for Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme; the 2026–2031 phase was announced as a Central Sector Scheme with an anticipated ₹565.50-crore outlay.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how interoperable, GIS-enabled land records can improve transparency and service delivery, while considering data quality, privacy and State-level implementation capacity.

- **Announced by:** **Department of Land Resources** on **9 September 2026**.
- **Guidelines:** Operational guidelines for **DILRMP 3.0 (2026–2031)** announced for launch on **10 September**.
- **Status:** On **9 September**, the guidelines were announced for the following day; the programme’s launch had **not yet occurred**.

# 2. Programme design
- **Full form:** **Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP)**.
- **Type and duration:** **Five-year Central Sector Scheme**, covering **2026–2031**.
- **Anticipated outlay:** **₹565.50 crore**.
- **Direction:** Shift from digitising records alone towards a **GIS-enabled “Land Stack”**.

national.headline: ICAR and ICRISAT announce Global Dryland Congress in New Delhi
facts: The government announced that the Global Dryland Congress 2026 would be held in New Delhi from 10 to 12 September.
The congress was jointly organised by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research and the International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics.
Its announced theme was “Transforming Dryland Agriculture with South–South Cooperation”.
The congress was expected to bring together more than 800 global experts to deliberate on six themes.
The event was scheduled alongside the 50-year milestone of the ICAR–ICRISAT partnership.
national.summary: ICAR and ICRISAT announced a three-day forum focused on dryland agriculture and South–South cooperation. The 9 September development was the advance announcement of an event scheduled to begin the following day.

national.prelimsTakeaway: The congress was jointly organised by ICAR and ICRISAT; its 2026 theme was “Transforming Dryland Agriculture with South–South Cooperation”.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss science-policy cooperation for dryland livelihoods, including climate-resilient crops, water management, land restoration and farmer-centred technology transfer.

national.headline: Foundation stone laid for BEDF Basmati and Organic Training Centre in Pilibhit
facts: The foundation stone for the BEDF Basmati and Organic Training Centre-cum-demonstration farm was laid at Tanda Bijeshi, Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh, on 9 September.
The centre is a joint project of the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority and the Basmati Export Development Foundation.
The planned facility is intended to provide training and demonstrations in Basmati production, organic cultivation, pest management and seed production.
The project also envisages support for farmer-producer organisations, entrepreneurs and startups seeking access to agri-export markets.
The foundation-stone ceremony marks the project’s start, not completion or operational status.
national.summary: The foundation stone was laid for an APEDA–BEDF training and demonstration facility intended to link farmer training, quality seed and organic cultivation with export support. The centre remains a project under development.
national.staticLink: Agricultural exports, farmer capacity-building, organic farming and agricultural value chains.
national.prelimsTakeaway: BEDF is the Basmati Export Development Foundation; APEDA and BEDF are joint partners in the Pilibhit centre.
national.mainsAngle: Analyse how training, seed quality and export handholding can improve farmer participation in value chains, while ensuring that export-oriented production remains sustainable and inclusive.

international.headline: WHO prequalifies multi-dose maternal RSV vaccine presentation
facts: WHO prequalified the multi-dose vial presentation of RSVpreF, the maternal respiratory syncytial virus vaccine marketed as ABRYSVO.
The multi-dose presentation is expected to make delivery more affordable and feasible, particularly in countries supported by Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance.
Maternal vaccination transfers antibodies to the infant before birth and is intended to protect the baby during the first six months of life.
WHO recommends maternal RSV vaccination from the 28th week of pregnancy or the use of the monoclonal antibody nirsevimab in national programmes.
WHO estimates RSV causes more than 3.6 million hospitalisations and about 100,000 deaths annually among children under five.
international.summary: The WHO prequalification adds a multi-dose presentation to the previously prequalified single-dose version of the maternal RSV vaccine. A more affordable and easier-to-deliver presentation may help countries expand protection for infants, especially where access to care is limited.
international.staticLink: Immunisation; vaccine prequalification; maternal and child health; global health equity.
international.prelimsTakeaway: RSV is respiratory syncytial virus; the prequalified product is the multi-dose maternal RSVpreF vaccine presentation.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how international vaccine quality assurance and lower-cost delivery formats can improve equitable access to preventive healthcare.

sources.title: WHO prequalifies multi-dose RSV vaccine vial, paving the way to protecting more infants globally
sources.publisher: World Health Organization

- **Date:** **9 September 2026**
| Presentation | Prequalification detail |
|---|---|
| **Single-dose** | Previously prequalified version |
| **Multi-dose** | Newly prequalified presentation |

- **Disease:** **RSV** means respiratory syncytial virus
- **Maternal vaccination:** Transfers antibodies to the infant before birth; intended to protect the baby during the first **six months** of life
- **WHO recommendation:** Maternal RSV vaccination from the **28th week of pregnancy**, or monoclonal antibody **nirsevimab** in national programmes
- **Delivery benefit:** Multi-dose presentation expected to make delivery more affordable and feasible, particularly in countries supported by **Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance**
- **Annual burden:** RSV causes more than **3.6 million** hospitalisations and about **100,000** deaths among children under **five**
> Exam angle: Distinguish the newly prequalified **multi-dose maternal RSVpreF** presentation from the previously prequalified single-dose version.

international.headline: Global report records at least 9,259 attacks on education in 2024–25
facts: The Global Coalition to Protect Education from Attack’s Education under Attack 2026 report covers attacks and military use of education facilities in 2024 and 2025.
The report recorded at least 9,259 attacks on education across the areas profiled, over 50 per cent more than in 2022–23.
More than 3,600 attacks involved schools; at least 10,600 students and education personnel were harmed.
A UN report on the findings said 258 million children in 87 countries faced severe learning disruption, while 93 million children were not in school.
The findings were highlighted on the International Day to Protect Education from Attack, observed on 9 September.
international.summary: The report documents a sharp rise in attacks on education and the military use of schools and universities during 2024–25. The figures underline the vulnerability of children and education systems in conflict settings and the importance of protecting education under international law.
international.staticLink: Right to education; children in armed conflict; international humanitarian law; SDG 4 and SDG 16.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The 2026 Education under Attack report covers 2024–25 and recorded at least 9,259 attacks, over 50 per cent above 2022–23.
international.mainsAngle: Examine how attacks on education deepen inequality and displacement, and discuss international and national measures to protect learning during conflict.

international.headline: WHO appoints Vanessa Kerry Special Envoy for Health Resilience
facts: WHO appointed Dr Vanessa Kerry as the WHO Director-General’s Special Envoy for Health Resilience.
The appointment expands her previous WHO role as Special Envoy for Climate Change and Health.
Her remit includes advocacy for integrated, resilient and sustainably financed health systems and stronger coordination behind national priorities.
The role includes a focus on climate-resilient health systems, universal health coverage, health workforce investment and sustainable health financing.
international.summary: WHO broadened Dr Vanessa Kerry’s envoy remit from climate change and health to health-system resilience. The role is intended to promote integrated systems, sustainable financing and preparedness for climate-related and other health challenges.
international.staticLink: World Health Organization; universal health coverage; health-system resilience; climate and public health.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Dr Vanessa Kerry was appointed WHO Director-General’s Special Envoy for Health Resilience on 9 September 2026.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss why resilient health systems require sustained financing, a capable workforce and integration of climate-risk planning into public health.
